blocks.text: Born in Vancouver in 1946, Jeff Wall trained as an art historian and came to photography through conceptual art. Since the late 1970s he has shown his photographs as large transparencies mounted on lightboxes, borrowing the scale of history painting and the staging of cinema. Some of his pictures are staged with actors and sets, others re-create scenes he has witnessed. Works such as “A Sudden Gust of Wind (after Hokusai)” (1993) and “A View from an Apartment” (2004–05) have made him a central figure of contemporary photography. He received the Hasselblad Award in 2002.
In this film, Wall discusses why his work shifted toward photography, and his lightbox transparencies are shown in his Vancouver studio.
